author: reek
body: This is the half that used to be invisible. missing-cite (beside this file) names a chapter that does not exist inside a quire that DOES -- that always threw, because the resolver knew where to look and found nothing there. This one names a quire the registry has never heard of, and the cite pattern was built out of the registry's own keys: an unregistered quire did not match the pattern, so the cite was never walked, the chapter was silently left out of the unit, and the author got a cascade of CDX3002 at every use site and not one word about the cite. The check that would have caught the mistake was made out of the thing that was missing.

author: reek
body: A whole quire was lost that way and nobody noticed: codex/workflow's chapters were cited as Wflow, which was not in the registry, so every one of them was dropped from every unit that asked for them.

author: reek
body: The test is worth as much as its failure. Before the strict pattern this file compiled clean and printed nothing -- it would have passed a test that only checked for a diagnostic somewhere.
